geometry.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate' confidence; no official hall-dimension figure was fetched to check this footprint against.

method: OpenStreetMap building footprint way 131496014 ('HERA Halle Nord', building=industrial), used verbatim. Its centroid sits 37.7 m from the HERA tunnel ring (geometry:hera-tunnel-ring) at the ring's north end -- consistent with a surface hall built over the underground North interaction point. Wikipedia's HERA page independently confirms 'H1 was ... located in the HERA Hall North.' This is the surface building; no source gives the underground H1 hall/cavern's own footprint, so this also stands in for detector:h1 and detector:alps-ii (both placed at this site).
name: HERA Hall North (H1)
notes: entity_id is the site (site:desy-hera-north-hall-h1), not the detector, following the same convention used on map:cern's Point-N boundaries -- the validator's map-entity-unaccounted rule scans entity_id, not site_id, and both detector:h1 and detector:alps-ii place at this one site id.

summary.plain: The surface hall over the HERA ring's North interaction point, home to the H1 detector (1992-2007) and now the ALPS II axion experiment.
